about.title: Personal Injury Help in Santa Clara, California
about.longDescription: Santa Clara sits at the center of Silicon Valley, and its streets carry a steady mix of commuters, students, and tech workers every day. In 2025, public records logged 367 injury collisions inside the city, with 496 people hurt and 4 lives lost. The corridors that show up most often in those counts are El Camino Real, Lafayette Street, San Tomas Expressway, and Monroe Street, and reported crashes tend to peak on Tuesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Behind each number is someone dealing with appointments, missed shifts, and an insurance adjuster who calls before the pain has settled. We understand that moment. Our team handles personal injury cases in Santa Clara County, and we work on contingency—no fee unless there is a recovery. You tell us what happened; we review your situation at no charge. If you decide to move forward, we handle your case directly. Whether you were hit while biking on Lafayette, rear-ended on San Tomas, or hurt in a fall at a Santa Clara business, the first step costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Santa Clara Claim

items.title: You generally have two years to file
items.desc: California gives most injury victims two years from the date of injury to bring a claim. If a city vehicle, a county bus, or another government entity is involved, the window can shrink to six months, so timing matters more than people expect.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were 20 percent responsible for a collision on El Camino Real, your recovery is reduced by 20 percent, not wiped out.

items.title: Pain and suffering are not capped
items.desc: In an ordinary injury case, California places no statutory ceiling on non-economic damages such as pain, lost enjoyment of life, or emotional distress. What you actually went through counts.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay nothing up front, and we are paid only if your case results in a recovery.

items.question: Do you handle Santa Clara personal injury cases?
items.answer: Yes. We handle personal injury cases in Santa Clara County, including car collisions, bicycle crashes, and slip-and-fall injuries. We work directly on your case and offer a free initial review.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Santa Clara?
items.answer: Public collision records for 2025 show El Camino Real, Lafayette Street, San Tomas Expressway, and Monroe Street as the corridors with the highest counts. Reported crashes also cluster on Tuesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are neutral record counts, and a crash anywhere in the city may still support a claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, California allows two years from the date of the injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a city or county vehicle, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months. Speaking with us early helps make sure no deadline slips by.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means your share of responsibility reduces your recovery in proportion but does not eliminate it. We can look at the police report and other evidence to sort out how fault is likely to be assigned.

items.question: What will it cost me to work with you?
items.answer: We work on contingency, so there is no upfront fee and no hourly bill. We are paid a percentage only if there is a recovery in your case. Your initial case review is free.
